title: Fitting a shower wall panel system over tiles
subtitle: Fit rigid PVC or acrylic composite wall panels over existing shower tiles to waterproof the enclosure and eliminate grout lines
excerpt: How to fit a shower wall panel system over existing ceramic or stone tiles. Covers measuring and planning the panel layout, cutting panels, applying panel adhesive, fitting corner and edge trims, and sealing with silicone.
sourceNotes: UK trade practice for wet-room and shower panel installation. Reader's Digest Complete DIY Manual (referenced, not reproduced).

glossaryTerms.definition: A flat composite sheet, typically 8 to 11 mm thick, made from acrylic, uPVC, or fibreglass-reinforced resin. It is waterproof and grout-free, designed to cover shower walls directly without tiling. Panels are bonded to the existing surface with specialist adhesive and joined with plastic trim strips at corners, joins, and edges.

A plastic extrusion used to cover the joints between panels at internal corners, external corners, and wall edges. The trim is fixed first with adhesive, then the panel edge is slid into the trim channel. Types include H-section (panel-to-panel joins), internal corner strip, external corner strip, and end cap.

content.text: Shower wall panels fit directly over existing tiles using adhesive, waterproofing the shower enclosure and eliminating grout lines. There is no need to remove the old tiles. BEGINNER: the work is measuring, cutting, and applying adhesive. The main risk is a panel that bubbles up: good surface cleaning and full adhesive coverage prevent this.
Measure and plan the panel layout
Measure the height and width of each shower wall. Note any obstacles such as shower valves and shower head outlets. Plan where

will join and what trim profiles are needed at each junction. Most panel systems use a maximum sheet width of 1000 mm: plan joins to sit at less-visible positions. Check whether the existing tiles are flat and securely bonded: any loose tiles must be re-fixed or removed before panels go on.
Clean and prepare the existing tiles

Degrease the tile surface thoroughly with a sugar-soap solution. Any soap film, limescale, or grease will reduce adhesion. Rinse and allow to dry completely. Key the tile surface lightly with fine abrasive paper to improve the adhesive bond: this is a quick, light pass rather than heavy sanding.

to the wall before the panels. Apply a bead of silicone sealant behind each trim and press it to the wall, checking it is plumb with the spirit level. Allow the silicone to cure before fitting the panels so the trim holds the panel edges firmly.

Mark cuts on the back face of each panel and cut with a fine-tooth saw or score-and-snap with a utility knife and straight batten. Apply panel adhesive in a grid pattern to the back of each panel, covering the full area and adding a ring of adhesive around the perimeter. Press the panel firmly to the wall, slide the edge into the trim channel, and hold or prop it flat for the time specified by the adhesive manufacturer.

Once the adhesive has cured, apply a continuous bead of sanitary silicone sealant at the base of all panels where they meet the shower tray or floor. Smooth with a wet finger. This seal is the critical waterproofing line: missing or broken silicone at the base allows water to track behind the panels.

attrs.symptom: Panel bubbles up away from the wall within a few days
attrs.cause: The tile surface was greasy or inadequately cleaned, reducing adhesion. Or adhesive coverage was insufficient.
attrs.fix: Remove the panel, clean both the tile and panel back with solvent cleaner, apply fresh adhesive with full coverage, and re-fix.

attrs.symptom: Water tracks behind the panel at the base
attrs.cause: The silicone bead at the base was not continuous, was too thin, or pulled away from the panel edge.
attrs.fix: Remove and replace the silicone bead. Remove all old silicone first with a silicone remover, clean the surfaces dry, and apply a fresh bead in one unbroken pass.
